questions.prompt: What new claim does Chapter 5 add about self-deception?
choices: It may help mislead other people more effectively, not just protect the self from pain
It only appears in clinical disorders
It means all motives are consciously hidden

explanation.gentle: The chapter says self-deception can serve a social function as well as a defensive one.
explanation.direct: Its key move is to add outward advantage to inward protection.
explanation.competitive: The blind spot can improve the public sell.

questions.prompt: How do older defensive theories differ from newer evolutionary ones in this chapter?
choices: Defensive theories focus on pain avoidance, while evolutionary ones add social advantage
Defensive theories deny emotion, while evolutionary ones deny motive
They are exactly the same account

explanation.gentle: The older view centers inner comfort, while the newer view adds better deception of others.
explanation.direct: The chapter contrasts self-protection with socially useful concealment.
explanation.competitive: One theory says shield the self; the other says sharpen the signal too.

questions.prompt: Why do modular minds matter in the chapter?
choices: They show that every thought is random
They make uneven access to motive possible inside one person
They prove people always know their true motives

explanation.gentle: Different parts of the mind can hold different information with different access.
explanation.direct: Modularity makes self-deception structurally possible without a single inner liar.
explanation.competitive: The head is not one transparent room.

questions.prompt: A manager sounds completely sincere while explaining a decision, but may not fully see the status motive shaping it. What chapter idea best explains that?
choices: Full introspective transparency
Self-deception improving the credibility of the outward signal
A total absence of motive

explanation.gentle: The speaker may feel honest because the strategic motive is not fully visible inside.
explanation.direct: Reduced motive access can make a public story look more convincing.
explanation.competitive: The signal gets cleaner when the actor misses part of the play.

questions.prompt: A student gives one spoken reason for a flashy move, while a coach suspects another hidden drive is also active. What mechanism is most visible?
choices: Modular access to motive inside the same person
Proof that the student is consciously lying in full
Evidence that motives do not matter

explanation.gentle: Different parts of the mind may not be sharing the full motive picture equally.
explanation.direct: The chapter uses modularity to explain sincere but incomplete self-report.
explanation.competitive: One process may know more than the spoken story does.

The whole self is always consciously faking ignorance
Motives may be partly hidden from the actor

explanation.gentle: The chapter does not need a single conscious inner trickster to explain the phenomenon.
explanation.direct: Its model depends on uneven access, not on a fully informed central manipulator.

questions.prompt: How does Chapter 5 grow out of Chapter 4 on cheating?
choices: It shows how concealment can move inward instead of staying only public
It says cheating disappears once the mind gets involved
It says norms no longer matter at all

explanation.gentle: The chapter turns fig-leaf logic inward by asking what happens when the actor also misses the motive.
explanation.direct: Self-deception is cheating logic relocated inside the self.
explanation.competitive: The cover moves from the act into the actor.

questions.prompt: Why can self-deception make outward behavior more convincing to other people?
choices: Because reduced access to motive lowers visible doubt and strain
Because people stop having motives entirely
Because observers automatically trust everyone

explanation.gentle: The person may show fewer outward signs of inner conflict.
explanation.direct: If selfish motive is blurred at the source, speech and expression can look cleaner.
explanation.competitive: Fewer inner tells often mean fewer public tells.

questions.prompt: Why does the chapter treat sincerity as real but not decisive proof of transparent motive?
choices: Because sincerity is always fake
Because modular minds and self-discretion can leave the actor partly blind to motive
Because motives never shape behavior

explanation.gentle: A person can feel honest while still lacking full access to what is driving the act.
explanation.direct: The chapter weakens naive trust in introspection without denying genuine feeling.
explanation.competitive: Clean sincerity can ride on incomplete access.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest bridge from Chapter 5 into Chapter 6 on counterfeit reasons?
choices: If motives stay partly hidden, the mind may start supplying cleaner explanations after the fact
Once self-deception appears, explanation disappears entirely
Counterfeit reasons matter only when people know their motives clearly

explanation.gentle: The next move is explanation-building from limited access to motive.
explanation.direct: Counterfeit reasons extend self-deception into post-hoc storytelling.
explanation.competitive: The mind starts writing the cleaner cover story.
